data_source: IMF World Economic Outlook via DataMapper (latest vintage, accessed October 2026)
inflation_management: The Bank of Thailand has targeted inflation since 2000 (currently 1-3%) and the record is strong: 5.5% in 2008 on the commodity boom, then 0-4% through the 2010s with mild deflation in 2009, 2015, and 2020, rising to 6.1% in 2022 before rapid easing to a projected -0.1% in 2025. The central bank hiked cautiously in 2022-23 and has faced political pressure to cut as inflation fell below target. Expectations are anchored; the current challenge is too-low inflation amid weak domestic demand, not overheating.
debt_management: Public debt was flat near 40% of GDP for over a decade (39.2% in 2006, 41.1% in 2019) on fiscal conservatism, then COVID pushed it to 58.4% in 2021 and continued borrowing has taken it to a projected 64.7% in 2025, approaching the 70% ceiling in the fiscal framework. GDP grew from $221.8bn to a projected $577.0bn. The debt is domestic and baht-denominated, and the government's borrowing headroom is narrowing rather than exhausted. Political pressure for stimulus (notably digital wallet handouts) tests the framework.

key_events.event: Military coup ousted Thaksin; political instability began.
Global crisis and domestic unrest; inflation spiked then collapsed.
Red Shirt protests and military crackdown in Bangkok.
Military coup ousted the Yingluck government; junta ruled until 2019.
COVID-19 devastated tourism (then ~20% of GDP); debt jumped to 49.4%.
Elections; Pheu Thai formed a government after the Move Forward party was blocked.
Tourism recovered; inflation fell below target, projected -0.1% in 2025.

outlook_next_decade: Thailand's base case is 2-3% growth on tourism recovery, EVs and electronics investment, with inflation hopefully returning to target and debt stabilizing below the ceiling. Structural drags are aging, household debt (near 90% of GDP), and political cycles that interrupt reform. Upside from supply-chain diversification (China+1) is real. Analytical assessment: macro stability is solid, but trend growth has downshifted and politics remains the wild card for fiscal discipline.
caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
